item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia - Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, North China's Inner Mongolia autonomous region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes.

item.title: Expert urges stronger climate adaptation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Expert urges stronger climate adaptation Report calls for locally tailored upgrade of infrastructure and lifeline systems A leading Chinese urban planning expert has called on the government to strengthen its adaptive capacity in the face of escalating climate-related disasters, highlighting transformative capacity and coping capacity as the most urgent priorities among core capacities. Li Xiaojiang, a national engineering survey and design master and former president of the China Academy of Urban Planning and Design, made the remarks following a study presented at the annual general meeting of the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development, a high-level international advisory body for the Chinese government, held on Sept 27-29 in Beijing. Li serves as the Chinese co-team lead of the CCICED scoping study on building a climate-adaptive society, which developed an assessment framework based on five core capacities for climate resilience: preventive, coping, recovery, transformative and long-term adaptive. The CCICED study comes as China pursues the goal of basically establishing a climate-adaptive society by 2035. It notes that climate adaptation has become a pillar of national security, sustainable development and public well-being, and recommends making it a mainstream consideration in planning, infrastructure, finance, technology and public governance. According to the study, coping capacity is defined as the ability to reduce disaster losses following extreme weather events. Transformative capacity refers to the ability of current social, economic and governance systems to proactively transform themselves into new systems with different characteristics when facing expected disaster risks. Li, a special adviser to CCICED, stressed that climate adaptation is fundamentally different from climate mitigation. While cutting emissions produces global benefits that are relatively easy to measure, adaptation responds to localized hazards whose types, timing, exposure and losses vary sharply across regions. "There is no universal template for adaptation," Li said. "There can only be lessons that are transferable among regions facing similar types of risks." For instance, a coastal city may face sea-level rise, storm surges and typhoons, whereas cities in central or northern China are more exposed to extreme rainfall and flooding. Meanwhile, the Chengdu-Chongqing region faces extreme heat, drought and mounting pressure on energy and water systems, he explained. The CCICED study's case studies examine Shanghai's exposure to sea-level rise, Shenzhen's challenges as a high-density city facing extreme rainfall, the Chengdu-Chongqing region's vulnerability to extreme heat, and the changing risks in arid northern China as some areas experience warming and wetting. Because of these regional differences, Li emphasized that local assessments are essential. Each region should evaluate its specific climate hazards, infrastructure weaknesses, and adaptive capacity, and then identify the most urgent actions. The study recommends linking climate adaptation capacity assessments with differentiated local strategies. Li pointed out that "transformative capacity" represents one of China's most important long-term gaps. Beyond repairing damage, transformation requires changing land-use decisions, construction methods and patterns of production and daily life. In extreme cases, the right choice may be to avoid areas facing unacceptable risks rather than repeatedly rebuilding in harm's way, Li said. He cited the reconstruction of Beichuan county in a different location after the devastating 2008 Wenchuan earthquake in Sichuan province as an example. "Relocation-based reconstruction should not be undertaken lightly, as it carries enormous costs and far-reaching social implications," Li stressed. "But that, in itself, is a form of transformation. It means not putting people and development back into danger, but proactively changing our approach so that long-term adaptive capacity can be built." He also emphasized the critical importance of lifeline infrastructure, including power, transport, drainage and emergency systems. Losses during extreme weather events often stem not only from the primary disaster, but from cascading failures such as outages, blocked transport and damage to underground facilities. The report calls for locally tailored upgrading and retrofitting of infrastructure and lifeline systems, including flood control facilities, energy and communications infrastructure, urban municipal facilities, transport systems, rural production areas and critical underground spaces. It also recommends revising engineering standards for climate resilience. Li urged policymakers to make full use of the new round of infrastructure investment to raise the quality and disaster resilience of China's built environment. He summarized existing weaknesses as low coverage, low standards in older systems, uneven construction quality and inadequate maintenance. Although adaptation projects may not always generate strong direct financial returns, Li noted that their national economic benefits are substantial because they prevent damage to lives, property, supply chains and broader economic activity.

item.title: 3 children, 1 adult killed in US school shooting: media
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
3 children, 1 adult killed in US Oregon elementary school shooting: media SAN FRANCISCO -- At least three children and one adult were killed Thursday in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, US state of Oregon, CBS News reported, citing law enforcement sources. Bend police spokesperson Sheila Miller said at a news briefing that police received a report at about 12:59 pm local time of a person firing shots into a vehicle outside the school. Within about a minute, multiple 911 calls reported that the gunman had entered the school and begun shooting. Police officers arrived at the scene and found the suspect shot inside the school. Authorities have not confirmed who fired the fatal shot. The suspect was shot and killed by a bystander, law enforcement sources said. Earlier, the police spokesperson said two people were transported to a local hospital with their conditions unknown. The total number of victims was not clear, Miller said.

item.title: China urges EU cooperation to promote trade ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
China urges EU cooperation to promote trade ties BEIJING - China hopes the European Union (EU) will jointly promote balanced growth and sustainable development in bilateral trade and maintain the stable and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said on Friday. Mao made the remarks at a regular press briefing when asked to comment on the latest developments in China-EU trade ties. The second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism has made positive progress recently, which shows that the two sides can properly handle differences through dialogue, Mao said. China hopes the EU side will honor its commitment to free trade and openness, abide by WTO rules, and avoid introducing protectionist and discriminatory policies and measures, she said.

item.title: New guidelines issued to regulate nursing home costs
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
New guidelines issued to regulate nursing home costs The central government has published guidelines to regulate the pricing policies of elderly nursing homes in order to let seniors get affordable, qualified and sustainable services. The guidelines are jointly unveiled by the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the National Health Commission. The guidelines clarify that nursing homes' pricing policies cover basic fees for beds and services, extra fees for diets and fees for on-demand home services. The government-sponsored nursing homes follow government-guided prices, and their pricing policies should be set by provincial-level departments or authorized city-level authorities. Commercial nursing homes are encouraged to offer high-quality services with favorable prices based on their running costs and people's demands, according to the guidelines. The guidelines have urged local authorities to optimize standards and evaluation mechanisms for nursing homes' pricing policies to make sure these policies are reasonable and transparent. For example, the pricing policies should be based on people's disposable incomes and the area's human resources costs. Also, the guidelines urge local authorities to improve guidance to nursing home operators and help them not only provide better services for the elderly, but also to prevent possible risks and settle disputes. Local authorities should cooperate closely with each other to crack down on improper or illegal behaviors such as not implementing government-guided prices or not marking prices clearly to secure the rights of seniors. As of the end of 2025, China had about 395,000 nursing homes and facilities nationwide with 7.68 million beds for the elderly, according to the civil affairs ministry.

item.title: Old department stores sell nostalgic journey to past
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
When Qiao Yanxiong was a boy in the 1950s and '60s, the neighborhood around Yong'an Road in Beijing was quiet and leafy. Neighbors all knew one another, and familiar local businesses catered to the daily needs of the community. The streets were lined with small shops and outlets — a laundry, a grain store, a bank and a bookstore. However, one emporium, the Yong'an Road Department Store, was the heartbeat of daily life. Qiao, 71, who now runs the department store, grew up nearby. As a boy, he shopped there with his parents for virtually everything. Nearly seven decades after the store opened on Jan 1,1958, he has one final goal. "I plan to work until 2028, finish the 70th anniversary celebration and then retire," he said proudly. Qiao remembers the department store as a place where shoppers could find almost everything they needed, from underwear and socks to pots and pans, bicycles and household appliances. The neighborhood and its surroundings have changed dramatically since those years. Many longtime residents have moved away, while supermarkets and online shopping have transformed the way people buy goods. The store's floor space has also shrunk. Its two main sales areas now occupy about 200 square meters, and its inventory no longer includes fabrics, bicycles and household appliances. But its identity remains deliberately old-fashioned, Qiao said. "Old store, old merchants, old products, old brands, old ways of selling and old ways of settling payments," he said. "The key word is 'old.'" In the past, one of its busiest sections was the fabric counter, a small space where bolts of cloth were stacked beneath clothing and quilt covers. A sewing machine sat behind the counter, and sales staff doubled as seamsters, sewing items for customers when business was slow. In the late 1970s and early 1980s, customers queued all day to buy fabric, particularly toward the end of the year when fabric coupons were about to expire. Even plain white cloth often sold out. The counter remained busy until the 1990s when ready-made clothes became cheaper with a wider variety.

item.title: Revolutionary spirit lives on in a new generation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Revolutionary spirit lives on in a new generation Ninety years after victory in the Long March, officers carry its legacy forward A pair of scissors snips carefully through a sheet of red paper. With a few precise cuts, the silhouette of a Red Army soldier takes shape. It is a tactile echo of a journey that took place some 90 years ago. In Huining, in Northwest China's Gansu province, history is never a distant abstraction. It is woven into the daily rhythm of soldiers like Xin Kaixuan, an officer in the Baiyin detachment of the People's Armed Police Force who leads a paper-cutting group with his comrades. For Xin, crafting figures of revolutionary veterans isn't just about preserving folk art; it is a way to bridge the gap between past endurance and present duty. Xin, who has loved paper-cutting since childhood, began creating works depicting Red Army soldiers and scenes from the Long March after joining his unit eight years ago. "Through paper-cutting, we can learn about the history of the Long March while passing on traditional culture in Huining," he said. "We also have calligraphy and reading groups, which give us more opportunities to learn about our history and culture." Ninety years ago in October 1936, the First, Second and Fourth Front armies of the Red Army converged right here in Huining, sealing the victory of the Long March. Today, a new generation of soldiers faces a different kind of march: not across freezing snow mountains, but through the quiet, demanding grind of modern service, community building and safeguarding a changing land.

item.title: Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary BEIJING -- President Xi Jinping on Friday extended congratulations to faculty, students and alumni of Hunan University as it marks its 100th anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a congratulatory letter to the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward fine revolutionary traditions, continue to elevate the quality and levels of its teaching, and strive to nurture more talent who can apply their knowledge to practical affairs, so as to make new contributions to building China into an education powerhouse and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1926, Hunan University has nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent over the past century.

item.title: New China-DPRK border bridge opens to traffic
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
New China-DPRK border bridge over Yalu River opens to traffic SHENYANG -- The new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge officially opened to traffic on Thursday, with both sides jointly holding an opening ceremony on this cross-border artery. The cable-stayed bridge over the Yalu River serves as a cross-border transport link between the city of Dandong in Northeast China's Liaoning province and the city of Sinuiju in North Pyongan province in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK). The double-pylon and double-cable-plane bridge features a 28.5-meter-wide deck designed with four lanes for two-way traffic, while its water navigation clearance is designed for vessels of up to the 3,000-ton class. The new bridge will further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said on Wednesday. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, and the new bridge is an important facility for connectivity between the two countries, Mao noted at a regular press briefing. Dandong boasts China's largest border trade port with the DPRK. Before the new road bridge, the Yalu River Bridge, also known as the China-DPRK Friendship Bridge, served as a combined road-rail bridge. The old one, however, could only accommodate trucks weighing no more than 20 tons for one-way road traffic. China and the DPRK in 2010 agreed to build a new road bridge downstream from the old one.
